series.title: TYPE THEORY — The Grand Unified Theory of Computation
series.thesis: Type theory is investigated as a candidate grammar of computational possibility: a language for specifying what computational constructions may exist, what information they require, how they compose, what distinctions they preserve, and what interactions they permit.
series.reference_baseline: Volume I RC1.1 reconciled publication baseline

volumes.title: JUDGMENT
volumes.subtitle: The Grammar of Computation
volumes.status: RC1.1 durably admitted reference implementation; external mathematical review pending
volumes.governing_question: What must exist before a program can even be meaningful?

volumes.title: COMPREHENSION
volumes.subtitle: How Computational Worlds Are Built
volumes.status: RC1 durably admitted; external mathematical review pending
volumes.governing_question: Which formation principles permit new kinds of computational objects and dependencies to exist?
volumes.formal_core: Dependent type theory through Pi, Sigma, families, inductive families, universes-as-preview, substitution and comprehension.
volumes.next_threshold: Proofs and programs as one constructive syntax.

volumes.title: PROOF / PROGRAM
volumes.subtitle: Logic Becomes Executable
volumes.status: RC1 durably admitted; external mathematical review pending
volumes.governing_question: Why do logical construction and computational construction repeatedly share the same laws?
volumes.formal_core: Curry–Howard beyond slogans: natural deduction, normalization, propositions-as-types, constructive logics, proof terms, extraction, parametricity preview.

volumes.title: PROTOCOL
volumes.subtitle: Computation as Communication
volumes.governing_question: What changes when the primary computational object is interaction rather than closed function evaluation?
volumes.formal_core: Session types, duality, linear resources, channels, process calculi, protocol fidelity, progress/deadlock distinctions.

volumes.title: EFFECTS
volumes.subtitle: Computation Meets the World
volumes.governing_question: How can types describe not merely returned values but the events computations may perform?
volumes.formal_core: State, exceptions, I/O, algebraic effects/handlers, monads, graded and capability types, probabilistic effects, recursion/partiality boundaries.

volumes.title: UNIVERSES
volumes.subtitle: Languages That Speak About Languages
volumes.governing_question: What happens when descriptions of computational spaces themselves become computational objects?
volumes.formal_core: Universes, codes/decoding, polymorphism, generic programming, reflection, metaprogramming, stratification and paradox avoidance.

volumes.title: IDENTITY
volumes.subtitle: Equality Becomes Structure
volumes.governing_question: What is equality when evidence of sameness itself carries computational information?
volumes.formal_core: Identity types, intensional/extensional equality, J, transport, higher identities, HITs, HoTT and univalence with computational caveats.
volumes.next_threshold: Multiple semantics for the same syntax.

volumes.title: SEMANTICS
volumes.subtitle: What Makes a Type Theory Mean Something?
volumes.governing_question: Which semantic structures validate type-theoretic rules, and which parts survive changes of model?
volumes.formal_core: Operational, denotational, categorical, realizability, game, domain, geometric and homotopical semantics; adequacy/full abstraction distinctions.

volumes.title: THE LIMITS OF CONSTRUCTION
volumes.subtitle: Computation, Incompleteness, Partiality, and Boundaries
volumes.governing_question: What do undecidability, incompleteness, nontermination, paradox, openness and physical interaction reveal about the limits of typed construction?
volumes.formal_core: Gödel/Turing/Church boundaries, strong normalization vs Turing completeness, recursive types, partiality, guarded recursion, oracles/open systems, probabilistic/continuous computation boundaries.

volumes.title: THE TYPE-THEORETIC SYNTHESIS
volumes.subtitle: A Grammar of Computational Possibility
volumes.governing_question: What strongest unifying thesis survives the previous nine volumes?
volumes.formal_core: Cross-volume synthesis of judgment, context, comprehension, substitution, construction, interaction, effects, reflection, identity and semantics; explicit residual counterexamples and open problems.
volumes.next_threshold: Research programme beyond the monograph collection.
